Replace the struck listing by the rule as it stands in lightning.spthy. It revokes the old states of both parties: the persistent !RevokedSecret facts are the knowledge, the linear RevokedCommitmentUnspent facts the one-shot outputs.

rule Revoke_Old_Secret:
    [ PendingA($A, $B, ptr, n_old, sAold, oldCommitA,
               n_new, sAnew, newCommitA, sigAnew, fA_new, fB_new),
      PendingB($A, $B, ptr, n_old, sBold, oldCommitB,
               n_new, sBnew, newCommitB, sigBnew, fA_new, fB_new),
      !Pk($A, pkA), !Pk($B, pkB) ]
    --[ StateUpdate($A, $B, ptr, n_new),
        Revoke($A, n_old, sAold),
        Revoke($B, n_old, sBold),
        Eq(verify(sigAnew, newCommitA, pkA), true),
        Eq(verify(sigBnew, newCommitB, pkB), true) ]->
    [ StateA($A, $B, ptr, n_new, sAnew, newCommitA, fA_new, fB_new),
      StateB($A, $B, ptr, n_new, sBnew, newCommitB, fA_new, fB_new),
      !RevokedSecret($A, n_old, sAold, oldCommitA),
      !RevokedSecret($B, n_old, sBold, oldCommitB),
      RevokedCommitmentUnspent(ptr, $A, $B, n_old, oldCommitA),
      RevokedCommitmentUnspent(ptr, $B, $A, n_old, oldCommitB) ]

notes.anchor: could add unboundedly many HTLCs on the same output.
notes.html:
We fixed it with a linear slot Mutex(ptr). Lock_Funds_And_Open produces it once, when the channel opens; Sender_Offer_HTLC and Forward_HTLC consume it when they add an HTLC on that channel; Receiver_Fulfill_HTLC, Intermediary_Settle, Sender_Timeout_Refund and Intermediary_Timeout_Refund give it back when that HTLC is redeemed or refunded. HTLCs are thus added to a channel one at a time, and the channel can be reused once its HTLC has resolved.

rule Lock_Funds_And_Open:
    [ ReadyToLock($A, $B, ptr, sA0, sB0, commitA0, commitB0),
      Wallet($A, ~fA), Wallet($B, ~fB) ]
    --[ ChannelOpen($A, $B, ptr), FundsLocked($A, $B, ptr),
        NewStateBuilt($A, $B, ptr, '0', ~fA, ~fB) ]->
    [ StateA($A, $B, ptr, '0', sA0, commitA0, ~fA, ~fB),
      StateB($A, $B, ptr, '0', sB0, commitB0, ~fA, ~fB),
      !ValidOnChain(ptr),
      !ChannelRecord(ptr, $A, $B),
      !ChannelConnect(ptr, $A, $B),
      !ChannelConnect(ptr, $B, $A),
      Mutex(ptr) ]

notes.html: Replace the struck sentence by: So we re-ran the whole of lightning.spthy after the fix (make verify): all 55 lemmas verify, namely 32 all-traces safety lemmas, 13 hop-bypass lemmas, 9 exists-trace lemmas found automatically, and Wormhole_Fee_Theft_Reachable, replayed from a saved 116-step proof.

notes.anchor: the guarantees of the concrete theory
notes.html: Replace "of the concrete theory" by "of lightning.spthy", and after "(Compromise_Ltk)" add: In addition, two compromised parties on the same payment can relay a preimage to each other around the parties between them (rule AttackerSkip, Sec. V-E).

For any two consecutive forwarders F1 and F2 on a payment with hash y (F2's incoming HTLC is F1's outgoing one): if F2's outgoing HTLC on y is redeemed and no party's key was ever compromised, then F1's incoming HTLC on y is never refunded, by anyone.

lemma Payment_Atomicity_Under_Liveness:
    "All F1 F2 Prev1 Next1 Prev2 Next2 ptrSF1 ptrF1F2 ptrF2R y #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(F1, Prev1, Next1, ptrSF1, ptrF1F2, y) @ #i
      & HTLCForwarded(F2, Prev2, Next2, ptrF1F2, ptrF2R, y) @ #j
      & Redeemed(ptrF2R, y) @ #k
      & (not Ex P #l. LtkCompromised(P) @ #l)
     ==> not (Ex Up #m. Refunded(Up, ptrSF1, y) @ #m)"

Since Forward_HTLC is one generic rule, F1 and F2 may sit anywhere on a route of any length; on a three-hop route ptrSF1 is the sender's HTLC and ptrF2R the receiver's. Sanity_Atomic_Payment_Completes shows that the premises are satisfiable.

notes.anchor: that forwarder’s long-term key was compromised.
notes.html:
Replace the struck listing by the statement in lightning.spthy (without the \_ escapes in the name):

lemma Intermediary_Never_Loses_Under_Liveness:
    "All P Prev Next Up ptrIn ptrOut y #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #j
      & Refunded(Up, ptrIn, y) @ #k
     ==> Ex #l. LtkCompromised(P) @ #l"

Lemma 2' (Intermediary Safety, strong form). If a forwarder's outgoing HTLC is redeemed while its incoming HTLC is refunded, then that forwarder's key was compromised before its incoming HTLC timed out.

lemma Intermediary_Never_Loses_Strong:
    "All P Prev Next Up ptrIn ptrOut y #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #j
      & Refunded(Up, ptrIn, y) @ #k
     ==> Ex #l #t. LtkCompromised(P) @ #l & TimedOut(ptrIn) @ #t & #l < #t"

Lemma 2' matches the honesty condition of T2b and T3, which bind a forwarder only if it is not compromised before its incoming HTLC times out. Both lemmas quantify over every forward, so they hold for every hop of a route of any length, in every trace that satisfies T1, T2b and T3.

Every forward on hash y is preceded by the HTLC it forwards: either the sender's offer on the forwarder's incoming channel, or the predecessor's forward that locked that channel's HTLC.

lemma Forward_Requires_Incoming [use_induction]:
    "All Me Prev Next ptrIn ptrOut y #i.
        HTLCForwarded(Me, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #i
     ==> (Ex S #j. HTLCOffered(S, Me, ptrIn, y) @ #j & #j < #i)
       | (Ex P0 pin0 #j. HTLCForwarded(Prev, P0, Me, pin0, ptrIn, y) @ #j & #j < #i)"

Because lightning.spthy has a single generic Forward_HTLC rule, this one lemma covers every hop of a route of any length, where a model with a fixed path needs one lemma per position (and an honest variant of each). It needs no honesty premise, because a forward consumes the linear Route fact, which only Sender_Offer_HTLC and Forward_HTLC produce. On the release side, Redeemed_Source and Fulfilled_Source state where a redemption and a consumed preimage come from:

lemma Redeemed_Source [reuse]:
    "All p y #i. Redeemed(p, y) @ #i
     ==> (Ex o. SettledHop(p, o, y) @ #i)
       | (Ex R Q. HTLCFulfilled(R, Q, p, y) @ #i)"
lemma Fulfilled_Source [reuse]:
    "All p x #i. UsedFulfilled(p, x) @ #i
     ==> (Ex #j. Redeemed(p, h(x)) @ #j & #j < #i)
       | (Ex #j. Skipped(p, x) @ #j & #j < #i)"

An HTLC is redeemed only by the receiver's fulfilment or by a forwarder settling that hop, and every preimage that a forwarder or the sender takes from channel p in order to settle comes from a redemption of the HTLC on p or from a wormhole skip (Skipped, Sec. V-E).

Lemma 4 (Fees Only on Success). A forwarder whose key is never compromised earns the fee of a hop only after it has forwarded on that hop and its outgoing HTLC has been redeemed.

lemma Fee_Only_On_Successful_Forward [heuristic={route_info_first}]:
    "All Me ptrIn ptrOut y %fee #i.
        FeeEarned(Me, ptrIn, ptrOut, y, %fee) @ #i
      & not (Ex #c. LtkCompromised(Me) @ #c)
     ==> (Ex #j. Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #j & #j < #i)
       & (Ex Prev Next #f. HTLCForwarded(Me, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #f & #f < #i)"

We prove no value-conservation lemma. Per hop, vIn = vOut + fee holds by construction (the Eq action of Forward_HTLC, Sec. V-A2), but amounts are not chained along the route: the offer, the invoice and the Route fact carry no amount, so we make no end-to-end value claim.

Replace the struck sentence on Multihop_Payment_Possible by: Multihop_Routing_Reachable shows an HTLC routed from the sender over two forwarders to the receiver, who fulfils it. Sanity_Honest_Payment_Completes and Sanity_Atomic_Payment_Completes show payments over one and over two forwarders that settle end to end, with no key compromise and no refund: every forwarder claims its incoming HTLC and the sender settles. The second witness satisfies the premises of Lemma 1.

Replace the struck sentence on Fees_Charged_On_Path_Possible by: Sanity_Compromised_Intermediary_Can_Lose shows a compromised forwarder whose outgoing HTLC is redeemed while its incoming HTLC is refunded, so the premises of Lemma 2 are satisfiable.

Replace the struck first paragraph by: Our model has three liveness restrictions (Sec. IV-A): T1 = RedeemBeforeTimeout, T2b = OutgoingTimesOutFirst and T3 = IntermediaryMustClaim. T2a is no longer assumed: ForwardTimeGap is a lemma derived from T2b and verified (Sec. IV-A).

Concrete block heights are treated in two auxiliary models of lightning_aux.spthy. With -D=CLTV, a positive CLTV delta (restriction DeltaPositive) leaves every forwarder a non-empty claim window: a preimage revealed before the outgoing deadline is revealed before the incoming one (Claim_Window_Nonempty), also over two staggered hops (Staggered_Path_Safe). With -D=CLOCK, channels carry concrete deadlines on a block clock, and nine lemmas (six all-traces, three exists-trace) cover the channel and HTLC lifecycle (e.g. No_HTLC_After_Close, Claim_Window_Exists, Loss_Implies_Skipped_Claim).

The four-rule model lightning_aux.spthy -D=TIMEOUT has no ordering restriction at all. There Tamarin finds the early-timeout race (exists-trace, 6 steps): a forwarder's incoming HTLC times out and is refunded, and its outgoing HTLC is redeemed after that timeout.

lemma Early_Timeout_Race:
    exists-trace
    "Ex P ptrIn ptrOut y #f #k #j #i.
        ForwardHTLC(P, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #f
      & TimedOut(ptrIn)     @ #k
      & Refunded(ptrIn, y)  @ #j
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & #k < #i"

In lightning.spthy the race is excluded for every forwarder that is not compromised before its incoming timeout:

lemma Timeout_Race_Blocked:
    "not (Ex P Prev Next Up ptrIn ptrOut y #l #i #j #k.
        HTLCForwarded(P, Prev, Next, ptrIn, ptrOut, y) @ #l
      & TimedOut(ptrIn)     @ #k
      & Refunded(Up, ptrIn, y)  @ #j
      & Redeemed(ptrOut, y) @ #i
      & #k < #i
      & not (Ex #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c & #c < #k))"

This is a two-sided check: the race is reachable without ordering restrictions and blocked in lightning.spthy. Timeout_Race_Blocked stays verified when any single one of T1, T2b and T3 is removed (Table III).

Replace the struck sentences by: We removed each liveness restriction in turn (make necessity: -D=NO_IMC, -D=NO_OTF or -D=NO_RBT, 600 s per check) and re-ran the five lemmas that may depend on them (Table III). Without T3, Tamarin finds a counterexample (exists-trace, 28 steps):

lemma Necessity_IMC_Honest_Intermediary_Loses:
  exists-trace
  "Ex S F1 R p0 p1 x #o #a #r #u.
      HTLCOffered(S, F1, p0, h(x)) @ #o
    & HTLCForwarded(F1, S, R, p0, p1, h(x)) @ #a
    & HTLCFulfilled(R, F1, p1, h(x)) @ #r
    & Refunded(S, p0, h(x)) @ #u
    & not (Ex P #k. LtkCompromised(P) @ #k)
    & not (Ex ptr y1 y2 #m #n. HTLCAdded(ptr, y1) @ #m & HTLCAdded(ptr, y2) @ #n & not (#m = #n))
    & not (Ex Me P q z #e. IntermediaryClaimed(Me, P, q, z) @ #e)
    & not (Ex A B C q z #e. SenderSettled(A, B, C, q, z) @ #e)"

No key is compromised, F1 forwards, R redeems F1's outgoing HTLC, F1 never claims its incoming HTLC, and S's HTLC to F1 is refunded: the honest intermediary F1 loses, which violates Lemma 2 and Lemma 2'. (The direct proof attempts of these two lemmas without T3 gave no result within 600 s; the counterexample is this separate exists-trace lemma.)

notes.anchor: So T3 is load-bearing for intermediary safety.
notes.html: Replace the struck sentences by: The two ordering restrictions are not needed in the same way. T1 is not needed by any of the five lemmas: all of them stay verified without it. T2b is not needed for intermediary safety: Lemmas 2 and 2' stay verified without it. We draw no conclusion from the cells of Table III without a result; in particular we do not claim that ForwardTimeGap or Lemma 1 needs T2b, or that Lemma 1 needs T3.

Replace the struck sentences by: Refund_Possible shows a griefing trace: after the invoice, the sender's HTLC is refunded and the payment never settles, with no forwarding and no key compromise. Since a refund requires a timeout (Refund_Requires_Timeout), the capital stays locked until then. This witness refunds the sender, not an intermediary. We report it as reachable griefing (denial of service), not as a new attack; it belongs to group 6 of Table II, marked (6) in Fig. 3b.

Replace the struck sentences by: Second, the model shows who can mount the attack. The wormhole is the attacker rule AttackerSkip (Sec. V-A2): two compromised parties on the same payment pass the preimage x from the exit party's outgoing HTLC to the entry party's outgoing HTLC, around the hops between them. Wormhole_Fee_Theft_Reachable (exists-trace; verified by replaying a saved 116-step proof) is the five-party trace of Fig. 4, marked (7):

lemma Wormhole_Fee_Theft_Reachable:
  exists-trace
  "∃ Alice Bob Att1 Att2 Indiana ptrAliceAtt1 ptrAtt1Indiana
     ptrIndianaAtt2 ptrAtt2Bob x #t1 #t2 #t3 #t4 #t5 #t6 #t7 #t8.
    (((((((((((((((InvoiceCreated( Bob, Alice, h(x) ) @ #t1) ∧
                  (HTLCOffered( Alice, Att1, ptrAliceAtt1, h(x) ) @ #t2)) ∧
                 (HTLCForwarded( Att1, Alice, Indiana, ptrAliceAtt1, ptrAtt1Indiana,
                                 h(x)
                  ) @ #t3)) ∧
                (HTLCForwarded( Indiana, Att1, Att2, ptrAtt1Indiana,
                                ptrIndianaAtt2, h(x)
                 ) @ #t4)) ∧
               (HTLCForwarded( Att2, Indiana, Bob, ptrIndianaAtt2, ptrAtt2Bob,
                               h(x)
                ) @ #t5)) ∧
              (HTLCFulfilled( Bob, Att2, ptrAtt2Bob, h(x) ) @ #t6)) ∧
             (SenderSettled( Alice, Att1, Bob, ptrAliceAtt1, x ) @ #t7)) ∧
            (Refunded( Indiana, ptrIndianaAtt2, h(x) ) @ #t8)) ∧
           (¬(Indiana = Alice))) ∧
          (¬(Indiana = Bob))) ∧
         (¬(Att1 = Att2))) ∧
        (¬(∃ #c. LtkCompromised( Alice ) @ #c))) ∧
       (¬(∃ #c. LtkCompromised( Bob ) @ #c))) ∧
      (¬(∃ #c. LtkCompromised( Indiana ) @ #c))) ∧
     (¬(∃ ptr1 ptr2 yy %fee #k.
         FeeEarned( Indiana, ptr1, ptr2, yy, %fee ) @ #k))) ∧
    (¬(∃ ptr y1 y2 #m #n.
        ((HTLCAdded( ptr, y1 ) @ #m) ∧ (HTLCAdded( ptr, y2 ) @ #n)) ∧
        (¬(#m = #n))))"

Alice, Bob and the intermediary Indiana are not compromised. Bob is paid and Alice settles, but Indiana's outgoing HTLC is refunded and Indiana earns no fee: an honest hop is bypassed. Conversely, a skip requires a key compromise:

lemma Skipped_Requires_Compromise [reuse]:
    "All p x #i. Skipped(p, x) @ #i ==> Ex P #c. LtkCompromised(P) @ #c & #c < #i"

The hop-bypass theorems First_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise, Second_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise and Hop3_ to Hop6_Skip_Requires_Compromise state, for the forwarder at position 1 to 6 of a route, that if the sender settles while that forwarder's hop is refunded (RefundHop), some party's key was compromised; they need no assumption on the number of offers but are proved in the full model, under T1, T2b and T3 (group 9 of Table II; Indiana in Fig. 4 is at position 2). Sec. VI extends this to routes of any length (Any_Hop_Skip_Requires_Compromise), for payments with a single offer; its conclusion, like that of the fixed-position theorems, says that some party's key was compromised, not which party or when. The PTLC subsection of Sec. VI shows, on the fixed route S, H1, H2, H3, R of lightning_aux.spthy, that per-hop locks rule out the attack around an honest hop when the sender is honest (No_Wormhole_Around_Honest_Hop), whereas the same route with a shared hash lock admits it (Wormhole_Around_Honest_Hop).
